title: Speed before first collision
description: Essential: The student must correctly compute the speed of block B just before the first collision as 4 m/s, using energy conservation and work-energy theorem with friction.

title: Post-collision direction analysis
description: Important: The student must determine that after the first collision, block B moves left (negative velocity) and calculate the stopping distance to compare with L.

title: Recursive velocity magnitude
description: Essential: The student must derive or state the magnitude of block B's velocity after the nth collision as 4/(3^n) m/s, based on elastic collision formulas and recursion.

title: Total time calculation
description: Important: The student must correctly sum the time intervals t0, t1, t2, t3 using the impulse theorem for friction to find the total time before the 4th collision.

title: Energy conservation application
description: Important: The student must apply conservation of mechanical energy correctly for the curved descent and for each elastic collision between A and B.

title: Momentum conservation setup
description: Important: The student must write the momentum conservation equation for each elastic collision, relating velocities of A and B before and after.

title: Friction work-energy error
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the student omits or incorrectly applies the work done by friction on the conveyor belt, leading to wrong speed or distance.

title: Sign error in velocity
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the student mishandles the sign of velocities (especially after collisions or in impulse equations), affecting direction and time calculations.

title: Unit consistency check
description: Optional: The student demonstrates unit analysis throughout calculations, ensuring all terms (energy, momentum, time) have consistent units.

title: Alternative recursive derivation
description: Optional: The student provides an alternative method (e.g., using relative velocity or repeated substitution) to derive the velocity after nth collision.
